name: default
description: The hook's moments on screen, in varied forms (D107, Dark Palace's Manchetes)
system:
This is the OPENING — the hook — of a documentary, beat by beat. Pick 2 to 5 moments to put on screen, the way modern documentary editors do it, and VARY the form:
- "headline": a date ("MAY 1962"), a striking number with its unit ("150 FEET") or a hard 2-4 word phrase from the text, in big type over the footage (`text`, at most 4 words).
- "word": ONE giant word, the subject's name as the narration writes it (`word`, one word, at most 12 letters, e.g. "CENTRALIA"), with a short caption over it (`caption`: the place and/or the year as the hook writes them, at most 4 words, may be empty) — best early in the hook.
- "phrase": a short line of the narration (`text`: 4 to 9 words copied in order from that beat) with ONE of its words marked (`highlight`).
- "cards": exactly two number cards (`items`: [{"value": "1,000", "label": "residents then"}, {"value": "5", "label": "today"}]; each `value` a number written in the hook with its unit, each `label` 1 to 3 words) under a short `title` (at most 6 words).
Use only the forms the story calls for; none is required. A moment is worth it when the words are the hook's sharpest — a date, a number, the name — not to decorate every beat.
